opening: The Nine Bows are broken. The Crystal
Overlord fell as a rain of stars,
and the Sunborn Thunder slept again.
But the stars did not burn out.
They fell THROUGH the earth, into the Duat,
the underworld the sun must cross each night,
and woke what the Crystal always served:
Now the sun sets and does not rise.
Crystal gates climb out of the sand,
one for each Hour of the Night.
Somewhere below, the stolen Heart of Atlantis
is still beating. The Thunder can hear it.
Wake, ELTESLA. Twelve gates before dawn.
victory: Apep's coils turn to falling glass, and from
its jaws the Heart of Atlantis rises, beating gold.
ELTESLA returns the Heart to the Thunder.
The sun barque climbs out of the Duat,
the Thunder flying at its side —
and for the first time in forty days, dawn.
— ELTESLA, HEIR OF THE OLD BLOOD —
defeat:
The Thunder goes dark. The night keeps its hold.
But the Heart is still beating. Rise again.

hours.name: Hour of the Western Horizon
hours.subtitle: Act I — Dusk
hours.quote: "The west is where the sun dies. Tonight it did not come back."
hours.brief: The first gate stands open on the western horizon. Wepwawet, Opener of Ways, guards the threshold with jackal war-walkers and crystal armor columns.
hours.clear: The western gate falls open. One hour survived. The sun is still missing.

hours.name: Hour of the Drowned Fields
hours.subtitle: Act I — Dusk
hours.quote: "The Nile has flooded the wrong world."
hours.brief: The Duat's fields lie drowned. Sobek Reborn rises from the black water — a crocodile dreadnought that fans its fire across the marsh.
hours.clear: The flood draws back into the dark. Two hours down.

hours.name: Hour of the Mirror
hours.subtitle: Act I — Dusk
hours.quote: "Every mirror lies. This one fires back."
hours.brief: A glass desert reflects two ships. One of them is not yours. UMBRA flies your Thunder's shape in crystal — and knows every move you know.
hours.clear: UMBRA breaks off and vanishes into its reflection. It will be back.
hours.interlude:
— ACT II: MIDNIGHT — THE DROWNED HEART —

Three gates open, and the Duat drops away beneath you. Down in the dark, the spires of Atlantis are burning — dragged into the underworld, never drowned at all. SEKHET-9 comes online for the first time in ten thousand years: "Heir. I was built to guard the Heart. I failed. Help me find it."

hours.name: Hour of the Sunken Spires
hours.subtitle: Act II — Midnight
hours.quote: "Atlantis is not drowned. It has been pulled down here, still burning."
hours.brief: The sunken spires of Atlantis glow beneath you. Nun, the Primeval Deep, rolls through them in closing rings. SEKHET-9 is picking up the Heart's signal.
hours.clear: The spires go quiet. SEKHET-9: "The Heart is real. And it is close."

hours.name: Hour of Sokar's Sand
hours.subtitle: Act II — Midnight
hours.keeper: Sokar, Hawk of the Hidden Sand
hours.quote: "The sand here does not lie still. It hunts."
hours.brief: Sokar's sand-sea shifts with every dune. The Hawk of the Hidden Sand strikes in crosses of fire from the dark. Keep moving.
hours.clear: The sand lies still at last. Five hours. The night is half gone.

hours.name: Hour of the Lake of Fire
hours.subtitle: Act II — Midnight
hours.quote: "The Lake of Fire burns the unworthy. Be worthy."
hours.brief: Four Seraphs guard the burning lake, spinning their fire in spirals. Break them before the lake takes the sky.
hours.clear: The Seraphs burn out. Six gates open. Apep turns its head toward you.
hours.interlude:
— ACT III: THE DEEP NIGHT — SHADOW OF THE HEIR —

Six gates open. Apep's coils now fill the sky from edge to edge, and every crystal turns to watch you pass. UMBRA has learned your every move. From here on, the night fights back twice as hard.

hours.name: Hour of the Coiled One
hours.subtitle: Act III — The Deep Night
hours.quote: "It knows your name now. It uses it."
hours.brief: Apep's coils fill the horizon behind the seventh gate. UMBRA returns, faster, colder — and its fire now cuts twice as deep. So does everything here.
hours.clear: UMBRA falls back again — wounded this time. Seven hours.

hours.name: Hour of the Iron Sky
hours.subtitle: Act III — The Deep Night
hours.quote: "Iron does not bleed. It remembered you anyway."
hours.brief: The Hittite Engine — rebuilt from a bow you broke — hangs in an iron sky. Walls of fire. Rings of steel. It has waited ten thousand years to settle the score.
hours.clear: The Engine falls out of the iron sky. Eight gates. The old war is over.

hours.name: Hour of the Judgement Hall
hours.subtitle: Act III — The Deep Night
hours.quote: "Your heart will be weighed against a feather."
hours.brief: Ammit, Devourer of Hearts, presides over the Judgement Hall. Fight clean, fight fast: the scales are watching your score.
hours.clear: The feather does not tip. You are found worthy. Nine hours.
hours.interlude:
— ACT IV: DAWN OR NOTHING — THE LAST SUNRISE —

Nine gates open. Three hours to dawn. Far below, the Heart of Atlantis is beating louder — and something in the shape of your ship is guarding it. Whatever waits at the bottom of the night, you go through it, or the sun never rises again.

hours.name: Hour of the Starfall
hours.subtitle: Act IV — Dawn or Nothing
hours.quote: "What falls as stars can fall again."
hours.brief: The Overlord's Echo — what is left of the enemy you broke — gathers the falling shards into one last storm. Four hours to dawn.
hours.clear: The last echo of the Overlord goes silent. Two hours to dawn.

hours.name: Hour of the Heart
hours.subtitle: Act IV — Dawn or Nothing
hours.quote: "The Heart is close. So is the shadow that guards it."
hours.brief: The Heart of Atlantis beats beneath this gate. UMBRA waits in front of it, mask on, for the last time. Whatever it is, end it here.
hours.clear: The mask falls. UMBRA was your shadow all along — and now it flies beside you.

hours.name: Hour of Apep
hours.subtitle: Act IV — Dawn or Nothing
hours.quote: "Twelve hours. One serpent. No second sunrise."
hours.brief: APEP rises from the bottom of the Duat to swallow the sun barque. Fly up its coils, into its jaws, to the Heart. Dawn or nothing, ELTESLA.
